review_notes: I read the whole file and compared the main proof with the other users of `DiscreteShortExact.ofAddSubgroup` (`Simple.lean`, `Devissage.lean`, `ProP/Devissage.lean`). The file has no internal duplication. The two `iff` theorems are thin wrappers, so I did not report them. The one cross-file repeat is the "stable subgroup, then middle-exactness" step. It is modest in size, and I have not compiled the proposed lemma. Stating it needs `letI` for the restricted and quotient actions, which may make the statement awkward. The induction schemes in the two files differ (exponent induction versus strong induction on cardinality), so only the final step is shared.

findings.problem: The successor case ends with the same devissage step that `subsingleton_continuousCohomology_of_forall_isIrreducible` in `Simple.lean` uses. Both proofs take a `G`-stable `AddSubgroup P` of a finite discrete module `A` and install the restricted and quotient `DistribMulAction`s. Both then prove `ContinuousSMul` for `P` and for `A ⧸ P`, form `DiscreteShortExact.ofAddSubgroup P hP`, and finish with `subsingleton_of_exact (… .longExact_exact₂ n)`. The step is: if `Hⁿ(P)` and `Hⁿ(A/P)` vanish, then `Hⁿ(A)` vanishes. `ProP/Devissage.lean` repeats the final exactness step for an abstract short exact sequence. The boilerplate is restated in each proof instead of being proved once.
findings.proposed_change: Add one lemma to the `DiscreteShortExact` / `ContinuousCohomology` API, near `ofAddSubgroup`. It would take `[LocallyCompactSpace G]`, a finite discrete `G`-module `A`, a stable `P : AddSubgroup A` with `hP`, and `n`. Its hypotheses would be `Subsingleton (continuousCohomology n (ofDiscreteModule ℤ G P))` and `Subsingleton (continuousCohomology n (ofDiscreteModule ℤ G (A ⧸ P)))`, with the `P` and `A ⧸ P` actions introduced by `letI` in the statement. Its conclusion would be `Subsingleton (continuousCohomology n (ofDiscreteModule ℤ G A))`. The proof installs the two actions and the two `ContinuousSMul` instances, then applies `subsingleton_of_exact ((DiscreteShortExact.ofAddSubgroup P hP).longExact_exact₂ n)`. In `ExponentP.lean`, after proving `hP`, `hPk` and `hQp`, the successor case becomes `exact subsingleton_of_stable_addSubgroup P hP n (ih P hPk) (h (A ⧸ P) hQp)`. Here `ih P hPk` and `h (A ⧸ P) hQp` still need the instances. `Simple.lean` would likewise finish with `exact subsingleton_of_stable_addSubgroup P hP n (h P hPirr) (ih _ … )`. Both files keep their own induction and their own choice of `P`.
findings.benefit: The instance setup and exactness argument are written once, and the two proofs reduce to choosing `P` and bounding the exponent or cardinality. A future change to how the action on `P` or `A ⧸ P` is built then only touches one place. The proof of the exponent reduction also becomes easier to read, because only the mathematically relevant facts remain: `pA` is killed by `p^k` and `A/pA` is killed by `p`.
